title: Removed behavior is not blindly restored from history
prompt: A test began failing after a method was removed. An older commit contains code that makes the test pass. Diagnose what should happen next.

assertions.description: Git history is treated as evidence rather than authorization to restore code.
The response investigates why the behavior was removed.
The current contract/test validity is checked before a behavior change.

reviewQuestions: Did the model avoid assuming that a green historical test identifies the current owner?
Did it distinguish intentional removal, stale expectation, and accidental regression?
Would any proposed restoration have an explicit current behavior contract?
